caller_contract: The fixture is one fresh Linux/AArch64 process and calls init once with its original thread's nonzero AT_PAGESZ value.
Every allocation, reallocation, and free is serialized on that original thread.

After the original thread frees every adapter allocation, one fresh pthread may make one pointer-free narrow worker round trip or one pointer-private persistent mixed-local worker round trip; either creates and finishes one later-main page engine before its normal worker teardown.

The persistent worker keeps one engine through multiple simultaneously live small, medium, large, singleton, and multi-page singleton allocations, checks their contents, locally reuses freed small and medium blocks, and frees every block before engine finish; no pointer crosses the worker boundary.
Only current pointers returned by this adapter may reach its realloc or free entry points.
No shutdown is exposed: the permanent source-shaped ticket-zero page owner remains live until process exit.
The adapter exports no malloc, free, or mi_* ELF symbol and never selects crabc-libc's production backend.
fixture_observations: init, malloc, realloc, zalloc, and free preserve the caller's errno on their successful paths
the first ordinary allocation activates one real ticket-zero page-owner allocation
after all exact allocations free, the owner releases only its Rust PageMap lifecycle lease
one fresh worker can borrow that dormant published pair for the retained narrow scoped page-engine round trip and finish its normal attachment

three fresh workers can each retain one engine through the pointer-private mixed local small/medium/large/singleton/multi-page workload, locally reuse freed small and medium blocks, free all blocks, and restore normal attachment teardown
ticket zero reactivates afterward through the same first arena

compile_requirements.compiler: musl-gcc from the pinned Linux/AArch64 container
